test_title: PYST 53: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 21 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the key realization that can lead to more sustainable use of natural resources?

options.text: Selfish exploitation causes environmental harm and misery
Only future generations must benefit from resources

solution:
The correct answer is __**Selfish exploitation causes environmental harm and misery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The core realization for **sustainable resource management** is that **unregulated selfish exploitation** of **natural resources** inevitably leads to **ecological degradation** and human suffering. This is often described in **environmental economics** as the **Tragedy of the Commons**.
 
• When individuals or entities prioritize **short-term profits** over **long-term stability**, they deplete **renewable resources** (like **forests** and **fisheries**) and **non-renewable resources** (like **minerals** and **fossil fuels**) beyond their **carrying capacity**.
 
• This exploitation results in **environmental harm**, such as **biodiversity loss**, **soil erosion**, and **climate change**, which directly causes **socio-economic misery** by destroying livelihoods and reducing the **quality of life** for present and future populations.
 
• Recognizing the **interconnectedness** of **ecosystems** helps society understand that **sustainable use** is not just an **ethical choice** but a **biological necessity** for survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development:** This concept was famously defined in the **Brundtland Report** (also known as **Our Common Future**) in **1987** as development that meets the needs of the **present** without compromising the ability of **future generations** to meet their own needs.
 
• **The Three Pillars:** Sustainability is built on **three interconnected pillars**: **Environmental Protection**, **Social Equity**, and **Economic Viability**. Focusing solely on **unlimited growth** (Option 2) ignores the **biophysical limits** of **Earth**.
 
• **Intergenerational Equity:** This **legal** and **ethical principle** suggests that **natural resources** belong to all generations. While **future generations** must benefit (Option 3), the realization must also encompass the **current generation's** responsible consumption to avoid **immediate misery**.
 
• **The Role of Regulation:** While **rules and legislation** are essential for **conservation** (Option 4), they are often insufficient without a **collective realization** and **cultural shift** toward **stewardship** and **voluntary compliance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Resource Depletion Data:** According to the **Global Footprint Network**, humanity is currently using **nature** **1.75 times faster** than our planet’s **ecosystems** can regenerate, leading to **ecological overshoot**.
 
• **United Nations SDGs:** The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, specifically **Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** and **Goal 15 (Life on Land)**, were adopted in **2015** to provide a global **blueprint** for mitigating **selfish exploitation**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The **Dasgupta Review (2021)** on the **Economics of Biodiversity** highlighted that our **global economy** is embedded within **nature**, not external to it, meaning **environmental harm** eventually results in **economic collapse**.
